summary: Independent verification phase (no production change, no implementation, no provisioning). Independently re-derives HRWP-001 v1.1, HRAC-001 v1.0, HBDC-001, current production source, and 2N.15/2N.16's own text fresh -- not accepted from 2N.17's own report, tests, or prose as proof. Verdict A: 2N.17's literal RP-ID rule (hatp.<operator-controlled-domain>) and origin rule (https://hatp.<operator-controlled-domain>) INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED as valid WebAuthn RP-ID/origin scoping for any legitimate operator-controlled domain -- effective-domain semantics, non-public-suffix precondition, stable operator control, no machine/IP dependency, certificate-issuance feasibility, and migration portability all independently confirmed. Single canonical origin confirmed for Mac/iPhone/future replacement hosts. Shared PCAE-wide HATP RP model confirmed not to imply cross-repository authority (enforced exclusively via RepositoryIdentity/DeploymentBinding/Principal/Signer/challenge binding). Physical-key-vs-credential distinction, DNS model, split-DNS optionality, DNS-01 (RFC 8555) mechanics, ACME trust boundary, certificate/TLS-key separation, certificate rotation, reverse-proxy/VPN/Host-header/Forwarded-Proto models, product independence (VPN/reverse-proxy/ACME client), migration model, DeploymentBinding separation, disaster-recovery state classes, authority-bearing-configuration classification, future HMIC-001 consequence, challenge-binding preservation, configured-origin/RP-ID source rules, RP-ID-migration and origin-migration consequences, and fail-unavailable behavior (no HTTP/IP/localhost/alternate-RP-ID/untrusted-origin fallback) all independently re-derived and confirmed against primary contract text and primary WebAuthn/DNS/ACME sources, not against 2N.17's own restatement. Both of 2N.16's Non-Blocking observations (Host-header/X-Forwarded-Proto trust rule; client-asset integrity classification) independently confirmed correctly carried forward by 2N.17, not silently dropped. Actual operator domain confirmed still unsupplied and not fabricated -- correctly not treated as a defect, per this phase's own governing instruction. Derived (not merely asserted) that the future literal RP-ID/origin freeze itself must receive independent verification before first credential registration, because a credential created under a wrong RP-ID cannot be retargeted by later config changes. Zero Blocking findings. Four Non-Blocking observations: port-policy should be an explicit requirement sentence rather than descriptive prose; a future domain-selection phase should freeze a mechanically-verifiable domain-ownership-evidence gate (e.g. scoped TXT record proof); origin-change-under-same-RP-ID should be explicitly distinguished in consequence from an RP-ID change; the Host-header/X-Forwarded-Proto gap remains open, correctly carried forward, not double-counted as new. 21 fresh, independent tests added this phase (not copied from 2N.16's or 2N.17's own test/doc modules), all pass. No RemoteWebAuthnProvider, no HTTP route, no DNS/TLS/VPN/reverse-proxy artifact, no credential, no HMIC change, no hac-dell mutation, no domain selected or fabricated. Fast Green: 342 failed / 8685 passed / 4 skipped / 9 errors unfiltered, identical to 2N.17's own recorded baseline, confirming pre-existing and unrelated; deselect-based clean re-run of all 351 failing/erroring node IDs: 8685 passed / 4 skipped / 0 failed. No hac-dell session opened.
